claims.statement: In the third year of Zhenghe of his reign the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual submitted the regulations for the empress's carriages.
ascended the throne (徽宗即位) and honoured Consort Zhu as Sagely Auspicious Imperial Grand Consort
On accession honoured the grand consort as Sagely Auspicious Imperial Grand Consort; withdrew the six-dragon palanquin but kept the dragon-and-phoenix palanquin and enhanced her other regalia.

claims.relation: used; built by edict for her welcome in the Shaoxing era

claims.statement: Welcomed back in the Shaoxing era; an edict ordered a dragon palanquin built for her; because she used the dragon palanquin the empress thereafter used only the eave-palanquin.
Delivered a dragon-eave palanquin with its full fittings to the Inner Palace for the empress's court audience.
In the Xianping era of his reign a palanquin with six traveling dragons was built for Empress Dowager Wan'an.

item.en: Great Peace Palanquin (her eave-palanquin, so named by edict)

claims.statement: succeeded to the throne (神宗嗣位)
On succeeding honoured the empress dowager as grand empress dowager, with processions following the Zhiping regulations and a palanquin like Empress Dowager Wan'an's.
As the late emperor, decreed in the Yuanfeng era that the empress dowager's procession escorts follow the daily precedent of Grand Empress Dowager Cisheng Guangxian.

item.en: palanquin with six traveling dragons, like Empress Dowager Wan'an's
item.zh: 如萬安太后輿，上設行龍六

claims.statement: Used only the secondary white-rattan palanquin for routine outings.

claims.assessment: modest and deferential (謙恭); did not ride the Great Peace Palanquin

provenance.sourceWork: Central Secretariat (中書) report of 紹聖元年

claims.statement: As grand empress dowager ordered the offices to review precedents, after which the grand consort's eave-palanquin was adorned with dragons and phoenixes and given a red parasol.
succeeded to the throne (哲宗既嗣位) and honoured Consort Zhu as imperial grand consort
Said the present empress dowager alone held supreme honour and could not be compared with Empress Dowager Xuanren; ordered the Great Peace Palanquin provided for her.

On the empress dowager's instruction ordered the grand consort to ride a six-dragon palanquin with a yellow parasol through the main Xuande gate; his decree weighed her honours between the empress dowager's and the empress's, and the dragon-and-phoenix palanquin was approved.

A Great Peace Palanquin was proposed and ordered for her, but she declined out of deference and it was never built; she instructed that the grand consort ride a six-dragon palanquin, and the consort used only a red parasol when accompanying her.

claims.action: conferred by Zhezong on his accession; allowed an eave-palanquin

claims.statement: Reported that princely and noble chariots all bore dragon ornament and asked that the regulations be reviewed; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office.
In the third year of Yuanfeng of his reign the Deliberation on Ritual Texts proposed revising the carriages and banners of the officials leading the procession; an edict approved it.

sourceDate.text: 其年 (the same year as 政和六年)

claims.statement: Argued that the order, carriages, and banners of the six escorts contradicted both antiquity and current practice, and proposed replacing the Minister of Education with the Minister of Revenue and the Director of Music with the Minister of Rites, reordering the escorts, and assigning Ink and Summer-Painted carriages and banners by rank; the proposal was approved.

claims.statement: From his time the great imperial procession had three escorts: first the Governor of Henan, then the Commandant of the Capital Garrison, then the Magistrate of Luoyang.

claims.statement: Showed favor to aged or ill imperial clansmen who could not ride, permitting them to use shoulder palanquins when going out and coming in.

Because officials did not yield the way when the Princes of Yan and Yue went out, they were granted a triple-jointed green-silk parasol, two large purple palm fans, gilt saddle and trappings, and gilt tea braziers, which became precedent.

Because officials did not yield the way when the Princes of Yan and Yue went out, they were granted a triple-jointed green-silk parasol, two large purple palm fans, gilt saddle and trappings, and gilt tea braziers, which became precedent.
During the Taiping Xingguo era of his reign grand councilors and commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs first began to use parasols.

sourceDate.text: 太平興國中 (the Taiping Xingguo era)

claims.statement: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo of his reign Li Fang, per edict, proposed saddle and bridle regulations, which were approved.

sourceDate.text: 太平興國中 (the Taiping Xingguo era)

claims.statement: Issued an edict forbidding parasols to all but the imperial clan.
In the second year of Xianping of his reign the Western Capital Remonstrance Bureau's request to forbid tassels to resident officials was approved.
Under the Xining regulations of his reign officials without rank were forbidden green canopies, and saddle fittings were graded by rank.
Issued an edict forbidding capital officials to use cooling fans.
In the third year of Zhenghe of his reign the Princes of Yan and Yue were granted a parasol, palm fans, and gilt regalia.
Said that while ministers escorted the court amid warfare, parasols should be temporarily waived and resumed when the imperial carriage returned.

Per edict to deliberate carriage and attire regulations, proposed that court officials of the ascending audience may use silver-fitted cord saddles, that sixth rank and below may not use ornate fittings or embroidered saddle cloths, and that commoners and officers be forbidden white-leather gear; approved.
Issued an edict forbidding ornate silver saddles to officials below fifth rank and regulating gilt-silver fitted saddles and bridles.
Issued an edict that when circuits, prefectures, armies, and directorates requested drums, horns, halberds, and spears, the Three Departments should act at once if the regulations warranted a grant.
In the fourth year of Tiansheng of his reign the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office advised against Fan Zonggu's request for spears for Guangan Army.
Memorialized requesting that spears be granted to Guangan Army; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office found army gates not listed in the regulations and advised against it.
Under the Yuanfeng regulations of his reign the number of gate halberds was fixed by prefecture rank.
Issued an edict that newly established commands and transferred headquarters receive banners and insignia arranged by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with bearers and horses supplied.
Ordered the banners and insignia of his former princely residence welcomed and installed in the Tianzhang Pavilion.
During the Chunxi era likewise ordered the Eastern Palace banners and insignia to be enshrined.
At Ningzong's accession a plaque was made for the banners and insignia of the Supreme Emperor's princely residence.
ascended the throne; the offices proposed enhanced ornament for enshrining the princely banners and insignia
